title: CostFlow Safeguard Orchestrator — automated conflict-resilient rollbacks & batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a lightweight orchestration layer (CostFlow Safeguard Orchestrator) that applies recommended batching and KV-cache configurations automatically, monitors effects on latency/cost/quality, and executes conflict-resilient rollbacks when guardrails are breached. This ticket covers the orchestration logic, trigger definitions, guardrail thresholds, reconciliation model for partial failures, and an explainable decision record for each automated action. The goal is to reduce manual toil for optimization changes while ensuring safe, auditable reversion paths when regressions or instability are detected.
comments: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff: aligned with PM and SRE on scope. Agreed to focus first on inference routing configs: batching params, prefix cache TTLs, and kv-cache hotkey limits.

2026-02-26 — Design review: opted for two-tier trigger model: immediate hard-guards (latency spike, error-rate) and soft-guards (cost per-token regressions, small quality drift). Marco to prototype reconciliation state machine.

2026-03-03 — Prototype demo: reconciler handles partial apply (30% of nodes failed) by marking config state as 'degraded' and starting gradual canary rollback across affected pools. Observability hooks added to Console metrics; PR#1245 opened.
2026-03-08 — Feedback from PM (Lina): require an audit record explaining why an auto-rollback ran and a suggested manual follow-up checklist. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10 — Security review requested. Waiting on answers re: secrets and KMS interaction during rollbacks for Private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can apply a recommended batching or cache config change with canary percentage control and store an immutable decision record.
Two-tier triggers implemented: hard-guards (immediate rollback on SLO breach) and soft-guards (rollback after configurable watch window and regression confirmation).
Reconciliation state machine handles partial failures: retries, pause for operator approval, or automated rollback depending on policy.
All automated actions produce audit logs with: timestamp, initiating recommendation id, metrics snapshots (latency/cost/error), and final outcome (applied/rolled-back/manual).
Console surfaces a per-change timeline and a link to the runbook with operator steps for manual remediation.

End-to-end e2e test that simulates: a) successful apply, b) partial node failures, c) induced latency regression causing immediate rollback, and d) cost regression causing delayed rollback — all validated in CI.
Security sign-off confirming no plaintext secrets are written to logs and rollback operations respect KMS/HSM policies for Private deployments.
implementation_notes: Architecture: small stateful controller in the runtime control-plane that subscribes to config-change events and recommendation stream from Optimize service.

Trigger rules: implement as pluggable evaluators. Hard-guard thresholds: p95 latency > baseline * 1.3 OR error-rate > 2x baseline for 30s. Soft-guard: cost-per-1000-tokens increases > 10% sustained over 10 minutes AND quality regression confirmed by eval-set mismatch > 2%
Reconciliation: state machine with states {pending, canary, degraded, rolling-back, succeeded, failed}. Persist to our existing config-store with optimistic locking + change-id + prev-state snapshot.
Rollback strategy: staged unwind — reverse canary -> pause -> full rollback. If partial hosts are unreachable, mark hosts as quarantined and continue with best-effort rollback while notifying SRE.
Metrics: emit trace id per change; record p50/p95 latency, cost tokens, error-rate, and key eval-set metrics pre/post. Hook into Console for timeline visualization.
Safety: include simulated dry-run mode which executes evaluation pipeline without mutating production configs. Enable for initial rollout to Dedicated and Private customers only.
Docs & Runbook: create Confluence design doc (link below), a runbook for operators, and a post-mortem template for any automated rollback that impacts customer SLOs.
